groups.title: Authentication and Account Access
groups.purpose: Sessions bind verified identity to platform or enterprise scope. Mandatory initial password change restricts access until saved; logout ends authorization without deleting business history.

groups.title: Customer and Workspace Management
groups.purpose: Platform Admin provisions one workspace per enterprise and its initial SME Admin. Staff accesses assigned setup metadata only; assignment changes never grant production-data access.

groups.title: Plan and Subscription Management
groups.purpose: Free and Subscription have fixed entitlements. Purchases retain quotes and only verified server-side payment applies rights once. Calendar validity uses Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, UTC storage and [start, expiry).

groups.title: Workspace Onboarding and Activation
groups.purpose: Specifications are retained for human configuration work. Staff readiness, Platform Admin handover approval and SME Admin activation are distinct recorded gates; initial Subscription starts only at activation.

groups.title: Enterprise Member and Permission Management
groups.purpose: SME Admin manages only own-workspace enterprise accounts and explicit field-view grants. Permission administration does not grant SME Admin plaintext access; history survives role/access changes.

groups.title: Detection Configuration Management
groups.purpose: Assigned Staff edits a versioned candidate containing fields, channel mappings and rules. Testing uses the exact revision and temporary samples; explicit application atomically changes one active version for newly accepted work.

groups.title: Integration and Transaction Ingestion
groups.purpose: Credentials establish integration workspace scope before mapping. REST, Webhook and production file import share normalization and atomic cross-channel business identity. Acceptance is durable and distinct from detection completion.

groups.title: Rule-Based Detection
groups.purpose: Free primary detection and Subscription fallback evaluate the selected configuration with the same typed semantics. All matching rules form one Rule Alert for the completed attempt; no match is distinct from failure.

groups.title: AI Detection and Rule-Based Fallback
groups.purpose: Subscription primary processing calls AI only. Unusable AI responses trigger rules and retain both attempt sources. Recovery reuses the transaction, checks historical event-time entitlement and preserves earlier alerts and cases.

groups.title: Transaction and Alert Review
groups.purpose: Operator reviews workspace production transactions, alerts and attempt history. Import results have separate SME Admin/Operator scope. Explicit reveal requires current field grants and, for Investigator, the relevant case assignment.

groups.title: Case and Investigation Management
groups.purpose: Only Operator opens cases from same-workspace AI Alerts under current Subscription. Assignment is separate from lifecycle. Existing case work continues after expiry; Operator may investigate, submit and confirm without a second person.

groups.title: Dashboard and Reporting
groups.purpose: Aggregates, reports and exports preserve workspace, role, assignment and field restrictions. Generation and download each recheck access; plaintext reveal does not authorize plaintext export.

groups.title: Notifications
groups.purpose: Relevant enterprise events produce minimal in-app/email content. Recipients and linked records remain scoped; external delivery is retried independently and never reverses or repeats the committed business effect.

groups.title: Platform Monitoring and Audit
groups.purpose: Platform Admin sees operational metadata only. Object history follows the underlying administrative, Staff-assignment or enterprise/case scope. Required local change history commits with the business action and excludes values/secrets.

paragraphs.text: This section presents the target detailed design derived from Report 3 functional requirements, Sections 3.2-3.15. Class diagrams identify controllers/listeners, service interfaces and implementations, repositories, DTOs and domain types. Sequence diagrams use the same class names and operations, with explicit calls, returns, activation bars and repository/database interactions. These proposed design signatures are not claims of implemented Java classes or approved HTTP routes; cross-module calls use public APIs/ports within the modular monolith.

All operations enforce current identity, role, workspace and object/assignment scope on the backend. Integration authentication establishes workspace scope before mapping or acceptance. Sensitive values remain protected in ordinary results and diagnostics; required writes retain history atomically. The headings named State Diagram follow the supplied reference: their figures use processing activities, decision diamonds, guarded branches and start/end nodes. Exact external wire formats, upload limits, timeout values and retry schedules remain subject to their confirmed interface specifications.
